title: Can You Say MIT's HARDEST Tongue Twister? 👅
description:
Say "pad kid poured curd pulled cod" five times fast, and your mouth tries to say two sounds at once. P is a pop at your lips; K is the same pop at the back of your tongue. Said slowly, they take turns. Speed up, and your mouth slips into an easier rhythm and fires both together: tongue sensors in speech labs have caught it making both at the same instant. That's why the first one is easy and the fifth falls apart. When MIT scientists tried this one on volunteers, some of them simply stopped talking. How many did you manage?

One idea for why this one is so hard: every word ends in a D, so the tip of your tongue taps on every word while your lips and the back of your tongue take turns, and the mouth would rather move them all together.
